what: Markel Group is a holding company built around specialty insurance. It underwrites risks the standard market will not take, invests the premium float in shares and bonds, and owns a group of unrelated operating businesses outright.
customers: Businesses buying specialty insurance and reinsurance, plus the customers of the manufacturing and services businesses it owns.
money: specialty property, casualty and professional lines
returns on an equity-heavy investment portfolio
wholly owned businesses in construction, manufacturing and consumer products
moat: An underwriting culture that walks away from underpriced business, combined with a long-term equity investment approach that compounds the float.
risks: Its large equity portfolio means reported earnings swing with the stock market
Reserve strengthening in its reinsurance lines has hurt results
Analyst targets imply the shares are already fully valued
opportunities: Markel Ventures now contributes meaningful earnings unrelated to insurance
Revenue grew about 10% a year over three years
A long record of growing book value per share
watch: The insurance combined ratio and growth in book value per share.
